clue.text: Old halfpenny returned for American coins

indicators.note: returned means the phrase for the old coin is read from right to left

parts.note: half of an old penny (d, from Latin denarius) can be called a semi-d

explanation.surface: A collector swaps a pre-decimal British coin back for some US small change.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 the British penny was written d, so half of it is SEMI + D; 'returned' turns SEMID round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is the American ten-cent piece, so several of them are US coins.

clue.text: Copy new plaid cut by East

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of plaid and cut are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A tailor reproduces a fresh tartan pattern, trimmed on the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PLAID + CUT into DUPLICAT; 'by' sets E for East beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy something is to make a second, identical version of it.

clue.text: Girl makes Eugene get up about one

indicators.note: about means the turned name goes round the other piece
get up in a down clue means the name is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Eugene Aram was a notorious 18th-century schoolmaster and murderer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman induces a man called Eugene to rise and walk around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' turns ARAM into MARA; 'about' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a fair example of a girl.

clue.text: Slim boy wandering in the street may be an artist

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters of slim boy roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A thin lad drifting along a road could be a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns SLIMBOY into YMBOLI, and 'in' puts that inside S...T.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Symbolism, a late-19th-century movement, were painters and poets using images to suggest ideas.

clue.text: Number going to castle- needs repair, they feel

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A count of visitors heads for a crumbling fortress that needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs repair' rearranges CASTLE into ACLES after TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's arms are its feelers, used to touch and grip.

clue.text: Fliers with big bills for meals?

definitions.text: Fliers with big bills for meals?

parts.words: Fliers with big bills for meals?
parts.note: reads like diners hit with large restaurant charges, but means tropical birds with huge beaks used for eating

explanation.definitionFit: These South American birds are known for enormous, colourful beaks that they use to pick fruit.

clue.text: Fail in court game?

parts.note: suggests losing a lawsuit, but describes a sport played on a court where one fails to get the ball through a ring hung from a net

explanation.definitionFit: A team sport, popular in British schools, where players shoot a ball through a high netted ring.

clue.text: Uncle Tom's boss turns up in India

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: massa is the old plantation word for master, as used in Uncle Tom's Cabin

explanation.surface: The slave-owner from Stowe's novel unexpectedly appears on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses MASSA; the definition 'in India' describes a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Old ale mixture should be warming

definitions.meaning: a traditional drink of hot spiced ale with roasted apples
fine soft wool from young sheep, used for warm jumpers

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an old hot punch of ale and apple and the soft fleece of young sheep, both comforting in cold weather.

clue.text: Declines to have writer aboard?

indicators.note: to have means the ship's letters hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: being on board is being on SS, a steamship
ink is what a writer writes with

explanation.surface: A reluctant author refuses to come onto the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords treat a ship as SS, so anything aboard sits inside S...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that declines drops lower, as a ship goes down or health falls away.

clue.text: Supreme type of Brazilian horse, perhaps?

parts.note: Para is a state of northern Brazil
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Asks whether a South American steed might be the very best breed.
explanation.walkthrough: Para is a Brazilian state, and 'perhaps' warns that the horse is only an example of a mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means highest in rank or importance, chief above all others.

clue.text: Some parsimonious male ?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a certain stingy man is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, standing in for a man in general.

clue.text: Princess appears to hail from U.S. state

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera
ho is a call used to hail someone

explanation.surface: A royal lady seems to come from somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ho!' is an old call to attract attention, as in 'Westward ho!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-western state of America, known for potatoes.

clue.text: Scaremongers disturb martial S.s. members

indicators.note: to disturb is to throw out of order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Rumour-spreaders upset uniformed members of a Nazi military corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturb' scrambles MARTIAL + SS; 'members' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmists spread fear, much like people who stir up panic.

clue.text: Concerns a group providing very loud tunes

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
airs are tunes

explanation.surface: Worries about a band blasting songs at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Business matters are one's concerns or dealings.

clue.text: Whereby future yields from gilts are expected.

definitions.text: Whereby future yields from gilts are expected.

parts.words: Whereby future yields from gilts are expected.
parts.note: sounds like government bonds paying interest, but gilts are also young sows, whose yield is piglets

explanation.walkthrough: Gilts are British government bonds; a gilt is also a young female pig, and her future yield is a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving birth to piglets is what this word describes, the litter a sow produces.

clue.text: Record timber yield from this tree

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
wood is timber

explanation.surface: A tally of timber produced by a particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American tree whose heartwood yields a dye.

clue.text: British statesman pleased with the new notes

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: new means the letters of notes are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A politician happy with freshly printed banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NOTES into STONE after GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was four times Prime Minister of Britain in the Victorian age.

clue.text: They fight with 28 in swirling dust

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the jumbled letters
swirling suggests the letters of dust are blown about into another order

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, a name

explanation.surface: Combatants face off with a rugby pioneer amid clouds of dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns DUST into DUTS; 'in' puts ELLIS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: People who settle quarrels by formal combat with swords or pistols.

clue.text: Irregular burst of tracer around one

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
a burst breaks something apart, so the letters fly into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gunner fires an uneven spray of tracer rounds at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst of' turns TRACER into ERRATC; 'around' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic is unpredictable and uneven in behaviour.

clue.text: Church to clean, perhaps, or part of it

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters of clean might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should tidy the whole church or just a section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CLEAN into ANCEL after CH; 'it' in the definition refers back to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a church near the altar, kept for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Sort of reading matter some find touching

definitions.text: Sort of reading matter some find touching

parts.words: Sort of reading matter some find touching
parts.note: sounds like moving literature, but means text read by fingertips

explanation.definitionFit: Raised dots that blind people read by feel.

clue.text: Matador plum?

parts.note: a star bullfighter could be a ..., which is also a wild fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A small wild plum, related to the damson, read jokingly as an ace with bulls.

clue.text: Maybe Jackson gets one point in 23

indicators.note: in means the other pieces go inside the word from 23

parts.note: the answer to 23 across
taken as written
W is west, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man called Jackson sits with a single point in a theatre seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is STALL; ONE and W go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewall was the nickname of Thomas Jackson, a Confederate general in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Drink in bed?

definitions.meaning: a sweet drink of fruit juice and spirit, such as rum
a woody bush grown in a garden bed

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both an old cordial of rum and juice and a bush planted in a border.

clue.text: Leave former tea combine

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: combine means the letters of tea are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Quit a defunct tea company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' rearranges TEA into EAT after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission for a pupil or student to be absent from school or college.

clue.text: Play for time in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a seat on the ground floor of a British theatre

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to stall for delay and the ground-floor seating of a British theatre, the stalls.

clue.text: Everyone coming round to see the coral reef

indicators.note: coming round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole party gathers to view the reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped island of coral enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Flower for poor Henri

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of Henri are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Blooms bought for an unfortunate Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is something that flows, so here a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A great European river flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.

clue.text: Numbers loving noisy get-together

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
amorous means loving

explanation.surface: A crowd of affectionate people at a rowdy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-together' only joins the pieces to the definition; the definition is 'noisy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means loud and insistent, making a din.

clue.text: Light music might be played?

definitions.meaning: a short, light piece of music
a table game rolling balls into holes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short trifling piano piece and a board game similar to billiards.

clue.text: NY island for William Webb, Rugby pioneer

definitions.meaning: an island in New York harbour, the old immigration station
the Rugby schoolboy said to have first run with the ball

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to the New York immigration island and the legendary founder of rugby football.
